authorization_note: Approved global maximum is 8 Kaggle quota-hours; Heat package proposes a hard 2-hour session/quota cap. It is not submitted or run.

quota_accounting.unit: Kaggle session wall-hour on NvidiaTeslaT4 machine shape (GPU T4 x2); reported independently of aggregate device GPU-hours

device_accounting.unit: sum of synchronized training and scoring seconds on each assigned T4

scoring.development: CUDA 257x129 after each of 15 Tier2 runs
scoring.confirmation: CUDA 512x256 for each of the 15 frozen final checkpoints after all training
scoring.expected_score_time: unbenchmarked; finite wave guards stop the campaign if actual CUDA scoring exceeds its allocation

device_accounting.arithmetic_device_seconds: 7500 Tier2 training + 360 smoke training + 900 development score + 30 smoke finite-check + 1800 confirmation score = 10590; held reserve 3810; cap 14400

planned_session_wall.arithmetic: 300 startup + 300 setup + 4000 Tier2 training + 480 development scores + 240 smoke training + 20 smoke checks + 960 confirmation scores + 360 process-wave overhead reserve + 40 artifact flush + 60 close margin = 6760 seconds planned, leaving 440 seconds under the 7200-second CLI cap
planned_session_wall.guard: The notebook timer starts in its first cell and stops starting work with a 60-second close margin; each process wave has a 20-second overhead reserve. Before every smoke/Tier2 wave the runner reserves all remaining Tier2 waves, all eight 120-second confirmation waves plus their overhead, artifact flush, and the 60-second close margin. Confirmation starts only if all confirmation waves and the 40-second flush fit. Kaggle CLI hard timeout remains 7200 seconds with 300 seconds startup reserved. The campaign records incomplete status if any allowance, checkpoint, or finite-metric requirement fails.

no_execution: No tests, validators, preflight, local training, Kaggle upload, or remote execution.
